clue.text: Giving affection, having a close relationship

parts.note: giving something over is handing it
love is deep affection

explanation.surface: Someone showing affection to a partner they are close to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving affection' reads as a second definition, but it is wordplay; only the closing phrase defines, and the letters are then regrouped 4,2,5.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hand in glove with someone is an idiom for working in very close association.

clue.text: Top teachers with sharp competitive advantage

parts.note: heads are head teachers, the top teachers in schools
tart means sharp or sour in taste

explanation.surface: Head teachers with a keen edge in competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an advantage given or gained at the beginning of a race or contest.

clue.text: Name Lennox, Hall and Oakley as childminders

parts.note: Annie Lennox the singer, Annie Hall the film, and Annie Oakley the sharpshooter are all Annies

explanation.surface: Naming three famous women as people who look after children.
explanation.walkthrough: The three surnames share the first name Annie, giving the plural ANNIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny is someone employed to look after children in their home.

clue.text: Tense remark made by a very conceited person!

definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense for continuous past action

definitions.text: remark made by a very conceited person!
definitions.meaning: a vain person might boast ..., which runs together as the answer

explanation.surface: A boastful person's remark makes everyone uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective, nervous; it is the grammar noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians name the past continuous tense the imperfect; the second reading splits it as I'M PERFECT.

clue.text: Rising star, for example, showing class

indicators.note: rising in a down answer means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the sun is a star
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A star on the rise shows real class.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a classification rank, a class or kind of things.

clue.text: Where I might put butter, having great success

definitions.meaning: butter spread on a bread roll is put ...

explanation.surface: Buttering bread while life is going well.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a roll is an idiom for a winning streak; literally, a bread roll is a place for butter.

clue.text: Former postman, one making a new life abroad

definitions.text: one making a new life abroad

parts.note: ex means former
Postman Pat is a British children's TV postman

explanation.surface: A retired postman emigrating to start afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat, short for expatriate, lives outside their native country.

clue.text: Feature about American's restraint

indicators.note: about means going around, so the facial feature wraps the letter

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
A is the standard abbreviation for American; the 's is just possessive dressing

explanation.surface: A characteristic of some American's form of restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain is a means of restraint, as for a prisoner or a dog.

clue.text: Provide e.g. food and support for future admiral, say

parts.note: to cater is to provide food and drink
a pillar is a supporting column

explanation.surface: Supplying food and backing for a young naval officer in training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admiral' is the red admiral butterfly, not a naval rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar becomes a butterfly, such as the red admiral, after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Fruit from two different trees

parts.note: the first of the two different trees is the pine
the second tree is the apple

explanation.surface: A fruit that seems to come from two separate trees at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The two trees, pine and apple, are set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineapple is a tropical fruit, though it grows on neither tree.

clue.text: A shocking swimmer?

parts.note: shocking reads as appalling but means delivering an electrical charge

explanation.surface: Someone who swims terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American fish stuns prey with a strong electric discharge.

clue.text: Bank bordering a street is better for consumers

indicators.note: bordering means lying on both sides of, so the bank encloses the other letters

parts.note: a tier is a bank, a row of seats or levels

explanation.surface: A bank by a street that serves its customers better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money; here it is a row or level, TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastier food is more pleasing to eat, so better from the eater's point of view.

clue.text: Dog that is following Antarctic explorer

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the abbreviation is placed after the explorer

parts.note: Captain Robert Falcon Scott led expeditions to the South Pole
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A dog trailing behind a polar explorer on the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottie is a Scottish terrier, a breed of dog.

clue.text: Many sheets of paper are rewritten, as well as manuscript

indicators.note: something rewritten has its letters set down again in new form, so the word are is rearranged

explanation.surface: Pages of a manuscript being redrafted on lots of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a quantity of paper, about 500 sheets, and reams means a great amount.

clue.text: Spreadsheet producer, fast and first-rate

parts.note: Excel is Microsoft's spreadsheet program
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Praise for spreadsheet software that is quick and top quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but is the noun: a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent and first-rate are synonyms, both meaning of the highest quality.

clue.text: Tick off one in the middle of scandal involving actors?

indicators.note: in the middle of places the numeral inside the combined scandal name

parts.note: the cast is the actors in a production
-gate is the suffix used for scandals, after Watergate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Reprimanding someone at the centre of a showbiz scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: A scandal involving actors would be dubbed 'Castgate', after Watergate.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to reprimand severely, and tick off is a British idiom for scold.

clue.text: Sew decorations on bride more extravagantly

indicators.note: extravagantly means wildly and without restraint, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: Adding lavish needlework to a bride's dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider is to decorate fabric with needlework stitches.

clue.text: Hints from prisoners about this, oddly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the prisoners wrap round the picked letters

parts.note: inmates are people held in prison

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the word this

explanation.surface: Prisoners dropping hints about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hints' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in 'suggests'; 'oddly' takes the first and third letters of 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to suggest or imply indirectly, so it is a verb synonym of hints.

clue.text: Criminal once more losing nothing — he often argued with the court's judges

definitions.text: he often argued with the court's judges

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the remaining letters are rearranged
losing means dropping a letter from the words once more

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A repeat offender who kept quarrelling with the judges in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes an O out of ONCEMORE, leaving NCEMORE to rearrange. The court is a tennis court; its judges are umpires and line judges.
explanation.definitionFit: John McEnroe, the tennis champion, was famous for disputing umpires' calls.

clue.text: Give name to capital in sheikhdom

parts.note: to dub someone is to give them a name or title
capital means excellent, A1, written with I for the 1

explanation.surface: Naming a capital city within an Arab state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests a city; it is the old exclamation of approval, A1, with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the emirates of the UAE, ruled by a sheikh.

clue.text: Unassertive person moving to road round motorway

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters surround the motorway letter
moving suggests the letters shifting position into a new arrangement

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A timid person heading for a road near the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges TO ROAD into DOORAT, which 'round' puts around M.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is a person who lets others walk all over them.

clue.text: Female with pride loses in running

indicators.note: running suggests letters set in motion and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A proud woman who loses a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' means a group of lions, not self-esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is a female lion, and lions live in groups called prides.

clue.text: Some scoff a liverwurst, or other meat products

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Eating liver sausage or similar meaty foods.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the edible organs of an animal, such as liver and kidneys.

clue.text: Seeing that transgression, curate loses heart entirely

parts.note: a sin is a transgression

indicators.note: losing the whole heart leaves only the first and last letters of the word curate

explanation.surface: A clergyman disheartened by a wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Since and seeing that both mean because, introducing a reason.

clue.text: Press old engineers to show where metal comes from

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Pushing veteran engineers to reveal the source of a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is the rock mined to extract metal, and iron ore yields iron.

clue.text: Football official earned corrupt votes

parts.note: a referee, or ref, controls a football match

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or twisted out of shape, so the word earned is rearranged

explanation.surface: A bribed referee earned money in a crooked way.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are popular ballots on a single question, so they are votes.

clue.text: Fashion line for Cara Delevingne, say

definitions.meaning: to fashion is to shape or ... something
Cara Delevingne is a fashion ..., so modelling is her line of work

explanation.surface: Cara Delevingne's career in the fashion world.
explanation.definitionFit: To model clay is to shape it; a model is also someone who displays clothes professionally.

clue.text: Is one tasked with picking up pork pies?

definitions.text: Is one tasked with picking up pork pies?

parts.words: Is one tasked with picking up pork pies?
parts.note: pork pies is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, and picking up means detecting

explanation.surface: Someone whose job is to collect pork pies from the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'porkies' or 'pork pies' means lies; a polygraph picks up lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygraph machine is designed to detect when a person is not telling the truth.
